english.title: Make luxury goods available for use in Russia
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) **(..SPECIFY DETAILS OF THE OFFENCE..)
english.legislation: Contrary to regulations 46B(2)(c) and 80(2) of the Russia (Sanctions) (EU Exit) Regulations 2019.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
directly or indirectly
made available for use in Russia
luxury goods

investigatoraction.description: Guilty Plea by letter procedure may be offered for this offence

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: It is a defence to show that the person did not know and had no reasonable cause to suspect that the goods were for use in Russia (see regulation 46B(4)(c) of the Russia (Sanctions) (EU Exit) Regulations 2019).

other.penalty:
England and Wales

Either Way
Summary: maximum 6 / 12 months imprisonment and / or a fine.
Indictment: maximum 10 years imprisonment and / or a fine.

The maximum penalty on summary conviction is 6 months for offences committed before 2nd May 2022; for offences committed on or after that date it may be 6 or 12 months depending on the general limit in a magistrates’ court, see regulation 80(2)(a) and (d) of the Russia (Sanctions) (EU Exit) Regulations 2019 and section 224(1) and (1A) of the Sentencing Act 2022.

Time limit for prosecutions
None
